differences: The paper reports behaviour as figures and Bayesian t-tests on baseline-corrected percent compensation (for example BF10 > 1e8 for the first versus last block of fixed-rotation training, BF10 = 0.447 for the mirror); these were not recomputed, so the published checks are the design numbers of Methods and Fig. 1 (participants, trials per block, targets, rotation sizes, mirror compensation levels). The OSF project states no license; the article itself is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, which does not cover the data.
